teachingQuestion: Which document type should express this security decision?
focalInsight: A policy establishes direction; standards make requirements measurable; procedures explain repeatable work; guidelines allow informed flexibility.
title: Security documentation: from direction to action
caption: Do not use a detailed procedure to substitute for management direction, or a policy to substitute for repeatable steps.

relationships.label: records an authorized variance from a named requirement

altSummary: Policy directs requirements and implementation. Guidelines advise. A documented exception varies a named mandatory requirement under the organization’s approval and review process.
textFallback: Policy establishes mandatory direction and accountability. Standards translate applicable policy into specific mandatory requirements. Procedures describe repeatable implementation steps; guidelines recommend adaptable practices. An exception identifies the particular mandatory policy or standard requirement being varied, the accountable approval, risk and compensating treatment, and the agreed review time or event. The standard link illustrates one possible requirement; document hierarchies and exception procedures depend on organizational governance.
